title: Finite presentation near a contracted prime for a finite type algebra from module-neighbourhood descent
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. For each commutative $k$-algebra $C$ write $C_K=C\otimes_kK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and for $v\in C$ write $C_v$ and $M_v$ for ring and module localization at $1,v,v^2,\ldots$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Assume the following neighbourhood-surjectivity principle [lem-sc-module-surjectivity-field-extension-neighbourhood]: for every commutative $k$-algebra $C$, every $C$-linear map $\varphi:M\to N$ of arbitrary $C$-modules, every $v\in C_K$, and every prime ideal $P\subset C_K$ with $v\notin P$, surjectivity of $(\varphi\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_K)_v$ implies that some $d\in C$ with $d\otimes1\notin P$ makes $\varphi_d:M_d\to N_d$ surjective. Let $A,B$ be commutative $k$-algebras and $\alpha:A\to B$ a $k$-algebra homomorphism. Let $\mathfrak q_K\subset B_K$ be prime, put $\mathfrak q=\{b\in B:b\otimes1\in\mathfrak q_K\}$, and let $u\in B_K\setminus\mathfrak q_K$. Assume that $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. If $(B_K)_u$ is a finitely presented $A_K$-algebra via $\alpha\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_K$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], then there is $s\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $B_s$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra.

proof.text:
Choose a surjection $\pi:T=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]	woheadrightarrow B$ with $n\geq0$, and put $I=\ker\pi$, using the finite-type hypothesis. The monomial description gives $T\otimes_kK\cong A_K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$: send $(a x^
u)\otimes\lambda$ to $(a\otimes\lambda)x^
u$; the inverse sends $(a\otimes\lambda)x^
u$ back to $(a x^
u)\otimes\lambda$, extended additively. Both preserve products, coefficients and variables. Write this ring as $T_K$.

proof.text: The $k$-module $K$ is flat. Applying flat tensor exactness to $0\to I\to T\xrightarrow{\pi}B\to0$ identifies $I\otimes_kK$ with the kernel $I_K$ of the surjection $\pi_K:T_K\to B_K$. Its image is the ideal generated by $f\otimes1$ for $f\in I$: every tensor is a finite sum $\sum f_j\otimes\lambda_j$, and $(t\otimes\mu)(f\otimes\lambda)=tf\otimes\mu\lambda$. Put $P=\pi_K^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$ and choose $v\in T_K$ lifting $u$; then $P$ is prime and $v\notin P$.

source.place: Tags 00F3 (definition-finite-type), 00R2 (lemma-finite-presentation-independent), 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); agent-written conditional finite-relation argument, with the module-neighbourhood principle assumed in the statement

proof.text: Adjoin one variable $y$. The localization presentation gives $(B_K)_u\cong B_K[y]/(uy-1)$. Consequently the surjection $\beta:A_K[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y]=T_K[y]\to(B_K)_u$, $y\mapsto1/u$, has kernel $H=I_K[y]+(vy-1)$. Indeed first quotient by $I_K[y]$, coefficient by coefficient, obtaining $B_K[y]$, and then quotient by $(uy-1)$. Since $(B_K)_u$ is finitely presented over $A_K$, the presentation-kernel theorem gives finitely many generators $h_1,\ldots,h_m$ of $H$.

source.place: Tags 00F3 (definition-finite-type), 00R2 (lemma-finite-presentation-independent), 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); agent-written conditional finite-relation argument, with the module-neighbourhood principle assumed in the statement

proof.text: For each $h_j\in I_K[y]+(vy-1)$ write $h_j=\sum_\ell a_{j\ell}(y)g_{j\ell}+b_j(y)(vy-1)$, with $g_{j\ell}\in I_K$ and polynomial coefficients; only finitely many terms occur. Express each $g_{j\ell}$ as a finite sum $\sum f\otimes\lambda$ with $f\in I$, and collect all these $f$ in one finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_r$. Evaluating $y=1/v$ shows every $h_j(1/v)$ belongs to the ideal generated by $f_i\otimes1$ in $(T_K)_v$. Conversely each $g\in I_K$, as a constant polynomial, is in $H$, hence is a combination of the $h_j$; evaluating shows $g/1$ belongs to that ideal. Thus $(I_K)_v$ is generated by $f_i\otimes1$. Here $(I_K)_v$ embeds in $(T_K)_v$: if $g/v^a$ maps to zero, some $v^b g=0$ already in $T_K$, hence in its submodule $I_K$, by the fraction criterion. This also identifies its image with the extended ideal.

proof.text:
Let $\varphi:T^{\oplus r}	o I$ send $(t_i)$ to $\sum_i t_i f_i$. Under $I\otimes_kK=I_K$ from Step 2, the scalar-extended map sends $(t_i)$ to $\sum_i t_i(f_i\otimes1)$; hence its localization at $v$ is surjective by Step 4. Apply the neighbourhood-surjectivity principle explicitly assumed in the statement, with $C=T$, this map $\varphi$, the prime $P$ and $v
otin P$. Obtain $d\in T$ with $d\otimes1
otin P$ and $\varphi_d$ surjective, i.e. $I_d=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)T_d$. Put $s=\pi(d)$. Since $\pi_K(d\otimes1)=s\otimes1
otin\mathfrak q_K$, we have $s
otin\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: Localization commutes with the quotient $B=T/I$, so $B_s\cong T_d/I_d$. Using $T_d\cong T[y]/(dy-1)$ and $I_d=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)T_d$ yields the explicit $A$-algebra presentation $B_s\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y]/(f_1,\ldots,f_r,dy-1)$. Thus $B_s$ is finitely presented over $A$, with the required $s\notin\mathfrak q$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finitePresentation_away_of_fieldExtension {k : Type u} {K : Type v} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] {A : Type w} {B : Type z} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] (hdescent : ∀ (C : Type (max u v w z)) [CommRing C] [Algebra k C] (M N : Type (max u v w z)) [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module C M] [Module C N] (φ : M →ₗ[C] N) (v : C ⊗[k] K) (P : Ideal (C ⊗[k] K)) [P.IsPrime], v ∉ P → Function.Surjective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers v) (φ.baseChange (C ⊗[k] K))) → ∃ d : C, algebraMap C (C ⊗[k] K) d ∉ P ∧ Function.Surjective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers d) φ)) (α : A →ₐ[k] B) (qK : Ideal (B ⊗[k] K)) [qK.IsPrime] (u : B ⊗[k] K) (hu : u ∉ qK) (hfinite : α.toRingHom.FiniteType) (hfp : ((algebraMap (B ⊗[k] K) (Localization.Away u)).comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.map α (AlgHom.id k K)).toRingHom).FinitePresentation) : ∃ s : B, algebraMap B (B ⊗[k] K) s ∉ qK ∧ ((algebraMap B (Localization.Away s)).comp α.toRingHom).FinitePresentation
